homes.name: Breezehome
homes.description: WhiterunLocated in Whiterun, right next to Warmaiden's and near the main gate, is Breezehome. The house has two stories, but is very small. However, Breezehome is the cheapest of all purchasable houses in the game and makes for an excellent starter home. The home's proximity to a blacksmith is very convenient for players who need Smithing amenities nearby.
homes.note: The cheapest home, and the only one that can never have an arcane enchanter.

homes.name: Honeyside
homes.description: RiftenHoneyside is a two-story house located in the northwest corner of Riften. The house is small, but slightly larger than Breezehome. One unique feature is that it has access from both within the city, and from a dock outside the city walls. This makes Honeyside a useful home for players who wish to avoid loading screens or players who are vampires as the house can be entered without attracting any attention or even venturing into the city.
homes.note: Has a garden and sits near an alchemy shop, which makes it the alchemist's pick.

homes.name: Vlindrel Hall
homes.description: Markarth Vlindrel Hall is located high above Markarth, in the northeast corner of the city. The house is spacious and, like the rest of the city, features Dwemer architecture. It can be upgraded to contain harvestable plants, display cases, three weapon racks, one mannequin, an alchemy lab, and an arcane enchanter. It has the largest amount of bookshelf space of any purchasable home, which is great for displaying your collection of books.

homes.name: Hjerim
homes.description: Windhelm In its most basic state, Hjerim in Windhelm features little more than a wardrobe, bed, and a chest. However the upgrades available for Hjerim make it arguably one of the most desirable houses in the game, featuring the largest amount of storage space, a large armory with several display cases, plaques and mannequins, and a large amount of bookshelf space. Hjerim also features a secret chamber, which can be turned into an Alchemy and Enchanting room. You must complete Blood on the Ice before you can decorate Hjerim.
homes.note: Ulfric won't let you buy here until you've helped the Stormcloaks take Falkreath Hold; on the Imperial side you must win the war first.

homes.name: Proudspire Manor
homes.description: Solitude Next to the Bards College in Solitude stands Proudspire Manor. Featuring three stories, it is by far the most expensive house in the game. The closest fast travel point is not Solitude itself but the Blue Palace. Despite its mammoth cost and grand design, the house is in many ways inferior to the other houses, featuring little storage space and no display cases.

homes.name: Heljarchen Hall
homes.description: The Pale, with the bedroom and kitchen wings The land for Heljarchen Hall lies north of Loreius Farm and west of Blizzard Rest. The land can be purchased from the Jarl of Dawnstar who resides in The White Hall. A unique aspect of this property is that you have the option of constructing a grain mill, allowing wheat to be converted into flour. This plot of land becomes available after you finish Waking Nightmare and Kill the Giant.
features: Built by you: choose wings such as an alchemy laboratory, enchanter's tower or library

homes.name: Lakeview Manor
homes.description: Falkreath Hold, with the bedroom, storage room, and armory wings South of Lake Ilinalta, between Falkreath and Riverwood lies the plot for Lakeview Manor. The land can be purchased from the steward at the Jarl's Longhouse in Falkreath. A unique aspect of this property is that you have the option of constructing an apiary, from which honeycombs and bees can be harvested. This plot of land becomes available after you kill some bandits.
features: Built by you: choose wings such as an alchemy laboratory, enchanter's tower or library

homes.name: Windstad Manor
homes.description: Hjaalmarch, with the enchanter's tower, alchemy laboratory, and library wings The potential location for Windstad Manor is between the Abandoned Shack and High Gate Ruins. The land can be purchased from the steward at Highmoon Hall in Morthal. A unique aspect of Windstad Manor is that a fish hatchery can be built to the north of the property, allowing you to breed and harvest varieties of fish. This plot of land becomes available after you finish Laid to Rest.
features: Built by you: choose wings such as an alchemy laboratory, enchanter's tower or library

homes.name: Severin Manor
homes.description: Raven Rock Severin Manor is located in the settlement of Raven Rock on Solstheim, and initially is occupied by Mirri, Tilisu, and Vendil Severin. It can be later awarded to you by Councilor Morvayn as a quest reward for Served Cold. Severin Manor is the only house you can own on Solstheim, and it features a number of differences from other houses in the game. Like many dwellings on Solstheim, it is mainly decorated with Dunmer-style furnishings.
features: Enchanting, alchemy, smithing and cooking areas, fully stocked
homes.note: No spouse, steward or adopted children can live here, and there's no housecarl.
